The demand for strong Controls Engineers has exploded, but the supply has not.

Companies aren't just looking for PLC programmers anymore.

They want professionals who can:

✓ Program and troubleshoot Allen-Bradley and Siemens systems

✓ Integrate robotics and automation equipment

✓ Lead startup and commissioning efforts

✓ Communicate with operations, maintenance, and management teams

✓ Manage projects while solving technical problems

The challenge is that the engineers who possess all these skills are already employed, highly valued, and rarely active job seekers.

When organizations take months to make hiring decisions, they often discover the candidate they wanted accepted another opportunity weeks earlier.

The best Controls Engineers don't stay available for long.

Pushing every single day to get better is a mindset challenge (just like athletes) especially when absolutely everything is changing from roles, processes such as spec driven development, tools, etc. This team were already smart and great partners but embracing this relentless journey was a new milestone so well deserved.
